Japan Factory Output Edges Up in July, Supporting BOJ Outlook
TOKYO--Japan's industrial production rose in July for a fourth consecutive month, signaling economic resilience as the central bank considers when to raise interest rates.
Industrial output rose 0.1% from the previous month, following June's 1.9% increase, government data showed Monday. A poll of economists by data provider Quick had projected a 0.8% decline.
Japanese companies expect industrial production to rise 6.4% in August and decline 4.2% in September, the data showed.

While inflationary pressures have boosted expectations that a Bank of Japan rate hike is imminent, policymakers are closely examining the impact of the Middle East conflict on corporate activity and the economy to determine the timing and pace of tightening.

Last week, Bank of Japan Deputy Gov. Ryozo Himino said the risk of supply shortages causing major economic downturns has diminished. The government has been making progress in securing oil from alternative sources other than the Strait of Hormuz.
